reading.title: Part 1: Reading - Blockchain Beyond Cryptocurrency
reading.reading_passage:
When most people hear the word 'blockchain', they immediately think of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin. However, the underlying technology has potential applications that extend far beyond digital money. At its core, a blockchain is a distributed, immutable ledger. This means that data is recorded across a vast network of computers, and once entered, it cannot be altered or deleted. This unique structure ensures unparalleled transparency and security.

One of the most promising applications of blockchain is in supply chain management. Currently, tracking a product from its origin to the consumer is a complex process plagued by fraud and lost paperwork. By using a blockchain, every step of the journey is recorded transparently, allowing consumers to verify the authenticity of their goods. Furthermore, developers are utilizing 'smart contracts'—self-executing programs stored on a blockchain that automatically run when predetermined conditions are met. These could revolutionize industries like real estate and insurance by removing the need for expensive middlemen.

reading.title: Part 2: Reading - Virtual and Augmented Reality in Training
reading.reading_passage:
Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) were once confined to the realm of video games and entertainment. Today, these immersive technologies are transforming professional training across high-stakes industries. While VR completely replaces the user's real-world environment with a simulated one, AR overlays digital information and graphics onto the physical world.

In medical education, VR allows surgical residents to practice complex procedures in a risk-free, simulated operating room. They can make mistakes and learn from them without endangering human lives. Similarly, in the aviation and manufacturing sectors, AR headsets provide technicians with hands-free, real-time instructions projected directly onto the machinery they are repairing. Despite the undeniable benefits, widespread adoption is currently hindered by the high cost of initial hardware and the complexity of developing custom software for these platforms. However, as the hardware becomes more affordable, immersive training is expected to become the industry standard.

reading.title: Part 3: Reading - The Rise of Edge Computing
reading.reading_passage:
For the past decade, cloud computing has dominated the IT industry. Data generated by user devices is sent to centralized cloud servers for processing, and the results are sent back. However, as the Internet of Things (IoT) expands, sending massive amounts of data back and forth creates a problem known as 'latency'—a slight delay in data transmission. For a smart thermostat, a one-second delay is unnoticeable. But for an autonomous self-driving car processing obstacle data, a delay of milliseconds can be fatal.

To solve this, engineers have introduced 'Edge Computing'. Instead of sending all data to a distant cloud server, edge computing processes critical data locally, right at the 'edge' of the network where the device is located. By doing so, devices can react instantaneously. While edge computing will not replace cloud computing, the two will work in tandem. The edge will handle immediate, time-sensitive tasks, while the cloud will be reserved for complex, long-term data analysis and storage.
